chapter_theme: The garb of austerity (தவ வேடம்): only those great in austerity can rightly bear the ascetic's garb, which the rest wear as hunters wear theirs; the chapter then lists the marks of the Siva-yogi, from holy ash and earrings to bowl, sandals and staff.
structure_note: One verse on who may bear the garb (1661), then three lists of the yogi's emblems (1662 to 1664), the last counting ten.

1661.reading: Those great in austerity are the foremost wearers of the garb; those great in futility are hunters bent on killing; those great in futility cannot bear that garb, which none but those great in austerity can carry.
1661.nuance: வேடர் means both 'wearers of garb' and 'hunters', and the verse turns on it: the false ascetic is a hunter in disguise. தவம் and அவம் (austerity and its empty counterfeit) are set against each other as in Kural 262.

1662.reading: Wearing holy ash is the first of the emblems; earrings of copper and the rudraksha string are Rudra's emblems for those who recite too; these are the emblems of the flawless Siva-yogi, if you examine.
1662.nuance: சாதனம் here means an emblem or outward means, not a practice. கண்டிகை is traditionally the rudraksha string. ஓதியவர்க்கும் may mean those who recite the scriptures, or those who have been instructed.

1663.reading: For the yogi there are the inner loincloth and the cloak, a single matted lock wound with cord, ash on the body, the skull-bowl, and the cane staff.
1663.nuance: The list is compressed and several words are unclear: உட்கட்டு, கஞ்சுளி, தோகைக்குப் பாசத்து, சீகந்தம், மாத்திரை. I take கஞ்சுளி as a cloak and பிரம்பு as a cane staff; the line divisions of the list are guesses.

1664.reading: Earrings, rudraksha beads, the horn, the good conch to blow, the high bowl, flawless sandals, the seat at the end of yoga, the flawless yoga band and the staff: these are the ten.
1664.nuance: நாதம் is taken as a horn or other sounding instrument, and கட்டி may be a separate item or part of the begging bowl (கப்பரை); the count of ten depends on which. யோகபட்டம் is the band that holds the knees in a seated posture.

links.note: Both say austerity's garb belongs only to those who already have austerity, and set தவம் against அவம்: for the Kural taking it up without it is futile, for Tirumular those great in futility cannot carry it.
Both make the false ascetic a hunter: in the Kural one hiding in a bush to snare birds, in Tirumular a வேடர் who wears the garb to kill, punning on the word for garb-wearer.

source_issues: 1663: line 3 reads நீறனி, probably for நீறணி; lines 2 to 4 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1661: line 3 கவர்வேடத் தாகாரவ் வேடந் is run together in the source; read as அவமிக்கவர் வேடத்தர் ஆகார் அவ்வேடம்.
